additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by a sense of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, fasting, overexercise, or misuse of medications to prevent weight gain. Self-evaluation is typically unduly influenced by body weight and shape, and individuals often oscillate between restrictive dieting and episodes of overeating. The course can be chronic or intermittent, with symptoms waxing and waning in response to stress, transitions, and changes in interpersonal or work demands. It is distinguished from binge-eating disorder by the presence of regular compensatory behaviors and from anorexia nervosa, binge-purge type, by the absence of significantly low body weight.

patient.stressor: Joan’s symptoms escalated during her second full year of teaching, when her school introduced a new literacy curriculum with aggressive benchmark targets that played directly into her competitive drive. In the months leading up to spring assessments, she began staying late most evenings to refine lesson plans, often skipping regular meals and then eating large amounts of food alone in her apartment while trying to unwind with knitting or reading. As her sense that she had to maintain a certain appearance as a young, high-performing teacher grew—especially after a casual comment from a colleague about "summer body goals" in the staff room—her preoccupation with her weight and shape intensified, and she started organizing her days around what she saw in the mirror and what the scale said. Over four months she increasingly avoided social activities, postponed planned quiet trips, and eventually sought psychiatric care after realizing that her mood, self-worth, and even her willingness to stand in front of the class were being dictated by how she felt about her body on any given day.
patient.chief_complaint: “How I feel about my body and weight is completely controlling how I see myself and how I function at school.”

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: Most mornings I stand in front of the mirror picking apart my stomach and thighs, and if the scale is even a pound higher I feel like a complete failure as a teacher and a person, to the point that I’ll change my outfit three times and still feel like I shouldn’t be up in front of the kids at all.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: After a big night of eating, I’ll punish myself by skipping breakfast and lunch the next day and then forcing myself to jog or do workout videos until I’m shaky and lightheaded, telling myself I don’t deserve to stop until I’ve “earned” back the calories.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: When I get home after staying late to plan, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have a quick dinner, but then I’ll end up plowing through an entire frozen pizza, a family-sized bag of chips, and whatever sweets are in the cupboard in less than an hour, eating way past the point of feeling uncomfortably full.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start eating like that in the evenings, it’s like a switch flips and I’m watching myself from the outside, thinking, “You need to stop,” but my hands just keep reaching for more food until everything in front of me is gone and I feel sick and ashamed.

add_requirements.binge_compensatory_frequency: Since the new curriculum ramped up around mid-year, I’ve been having these huge nighttime eating blowouts and then doing some mix of fasting and overexercising to make up for it at least a few times every week, usually four or five nights out of seven.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: My energy and focus at school have tanked because I’m either wiped out from binging or dizzy from overexercising and skipping meals, so I’ve started calling in sick more often and avoiding staff gatherings because I’m embarrassed about how out of control I feel around food and my body.
add_requirements.duration: This pattern of out-of-control evening eating and extreme “make up” days has been going on for about four months, ever since the pressure around the new literacy benchmarks kicked in.
